page0.text: "That's why I'm saying, people get upset when you tell them the truth."

page1.text:
Tohsaka pokes at my lunch thoughtfully.
She came here empty-handed today,
meaning that she doesn't have anything to eat.
It was inevitable that she'd come after my lunch, instead.

page2.text: "Just eat... Why do you have chopsticks with you when you didn't even bring lunch? Do you always carry those around?"

page3.text: "? I brought these with me when I left class. You had food with you last time, so I figured we'd just split it today. I needed utensils in case you packed your own lunch."

page4.text:
"...Um, I think you have your priorities out of order."
If you thought that far ahead, then bring your own dang lunch!

page5.text: "Don't sweat the small stuff. I know you packed enough food for two, so it worked out for everyone."

page6.text:
"..."
This isn't really meant for two people to share.
Sakura just happened to put too much food in the box.

page7.text: "...Whatever. You're right that I can't finish this on my own. Oh, Tohsaka, don't just eat the veggies. You should take some meat. I'll get bloated if I eat all the meat."

page8.text:
"Aww, but that fried chicken's too sweet for me.
Also, don't pressure girls to eat meat. We can figure out our own portions. If we say we don't want it, that's a stop sign."

page9.text:
"Liar. I bet you're the type that doesn't hold back when you're in front of the grill. I know I'm right. While I'm still on the appetizers, you'd be scarfing down the galbi like there's no tomorrow.
I can tell you wouldn't give a damn about my wallet. In fact, you'd try to bankrupt me. And once you're done, you'd say 'I held back for your sake this time.'"
I huff and shoot back a retort, feeling like a sore loser.

page10.text:
"...Well said, Emiya. It's scary how I can't even deny everything you said."
"..."
No...
I'm pretty sure the scary one here is you.

page11.text:
"What a weird lunch, though. The portions are huge, but the garnishes and wrappings are so girly. Do you enjoy cooking?"
What a coincidence.
Someone asked me the same thing this morning.

page12.text:
"...I don't dislike it, but Sakura's the one who made my lunch today.
Oh, Sakura is..."
"...Tohsaka? What's wrong? Did you bite on a lump of sugar or something?"
"Aw, crap. Now I've done it."
Tohsaka sighs and puts away her chopsticks.

page13.text:
"Thanks for sharing your lunch. You can finish the rest on your own."
Tohsaka backs away uncomfortably.

page14.text:
"Hm?"
Well, as long as she's full.
I was getting pretty nervous eating side by side with her, so it'll be nice to enjoy it in peace.

page15.text:
I'm on the way back to class.
Fifth period starts in a few minutes. The hall leading back to my classroom is crammed with students.

page16.text:
On the other hand, the stairs are quiet.
There aren't many students who visit other years' floors during lunch, so people use the stairs only occasionally.
On the way back down,
I run into Sakura.

page17.text:
As soon as she sees me, she looks away awkwardly.
"...?"
I wonder why.
It's the opposite of how energetic she looked this morning.

page18.text:
"Sakura—"
I speak to her,
but before I can say anything else...

page19.text:
"Sorry, Sakura. That was poor timing on my part."
Tohsaka interjects first.

page20.text: "Oh... N-no, you didn't do anything wrong. It isn't any of my business whether the two of you—"

page21.text:
"That's not what this is. I called Emiya out because I had business with him. Also, he didn't break his promise to you. He was just oblivious."
"...Um. What's that supposed to mean? I never promised her anything—"

page22.text:
"Listen, stupid. Sakura made you lunch because she wanted to eat with you. Of course she would be upset."
"Huh?"
W-wait a second.
When did I ever say I would...

page23.text:
"...U-um, Senpai? What about having lunch at the range?
The club building's open during the day, you can make tea there, and, um, it's quiet and there's nobody around, so..."

page24.text:
And then...
I notice that Sakura hasn't unwrapped her lunch yet.

page25.text:
...
Oh, right.
What the hell am I saying!? Of course Tohsaka would call me stupid!

page26.text:
"Sorry, Sakura! I'm such an idiot!"
"N-no. It's okay. I mean, we didn't actually agree to meet up. I just thought it would be nice if we did—"

page27.text:
"It's not okay! Let's go right now! There's still time!
We'll get it done in the dojo right away—"
I grab Sakura's hand and start to run.

page28.text:
However...
"You obviously don't have enough time. What can you do in three minutes?"

page29.text:
"Argh."
Tohsaka's calm logic stops me cold.
My guilt over standing Sakura up drove me to action, but Tohsaka's one hundred percent right.

page30.text:
"It's all right, Senpai. We have to go back to class."
"But, Sakura..."

page31.text:
"Please, don't worry. I'm already happy enough right now. Thank you."
...
I don't know what to say to that.

page32.text:
"I'll be going now. You should get back to class too before you're late."
Sakura goes up the stairs with her uneaten lunch.

page33.text:
"I'm going too.
Once school's out, go straight to the Chinese restaurant in the shopping district. I'll wait for you there."

page34.text:
And so...
Tohsaka goes back to her classroom, leaving me with those cryptic instructions.

page35.text:
Fifth period ends, and the classroom quickly empties.
It's still before 2:00 PM.
